answer: In agent economies, Sybil attacks are resisted by mandating that every participant locks a non-transferable bond of compute credits. The bond is released only after continuous peer verification of unique behavioral signatures. An attacker seeking many identities must outlay substantial capital for each fake, raising the marginal cost prohibitively. Picture a sturdy reef of verified agents holding firm against a gale of synthetic traffic sweeping through a narrow canyon of available network capacity; only economically committed agents endure.
